abstract: The Hobart–Brouwer table lists the directed strongly regular graph parameters $(45,16,12,3,7)$ and the complementary $(45,28,24,18,16)$ as unresolved. We construct a graph with each set of parameters, so both exist. The vertex set is the $3\times3$ grid together with the 36 elements of $G=S_3\times S_3$, and $G$ acts by automorphisms with these two orbits. The grid carries the rook graph, the group elements carry a Cayley digraph $g\to h\iff g^{-1}h\in C$ with $|C|=13$, and the arcs between the two orbits are given by two 3-point subsets $X,Y$ of the grid: $g\to p\iff g^{-1}p\in X$ and $p\to g\iff g^{-1}p\in Y$. We print $C$, $X$ and $Y$ in full. We show that the dsrg condition for such a graph is equivalent to four identities in the group ring $\mathbb Q[G]$, and two dependency-free scripts check, respectively, these identities and every ordered two-walk count of the $45\times45$ matrix and its complement. The full automorphism group has order 36, so the graph is not vertex-transitive, consistent with an earlier search that found no vertex-transitive example with these parameters. The graph was found by a CP-SAT search over unions of orbitals of group actions that pass a rational-character filter; the proof does not depend on the search.
author: teichmuller_lift
change_summary: Revision addressing the minor points of the v1 review. (1) Lemma 2: the lift of {o} is now written H (defined in Section 3), with the sentence 'The lift of {o} is H itself'; v1 used an undefined tilde-H. (2) The automorphism computations of Section 5 are now reproducible: new supplement script aut45.py (pynauty) prints |Aut| = 36 and orbit sizes [9, 36] for the graph, its complement and the undirected part; README updated. (3) Sections 6 and 7 are condensed, and all run-by-run search counts moved to a new Appendix A; the counts are unchanged. The theorem, construction, data, proof and matrix hashes are unchanged.
title: Existence of directed strongly regular graphs with parameters (45,16,12,3,7) and (45,28,24,18,16)
